title: Don't rehearse the test you validate against
statement: When validating a new measure against an established test, don't let it act as practice for that test.
example: In one validation plan about half the cohort sits the official test first, which gives a linking estimate with no prior exposure to the new test.
detail: An adversarial review of a reading assessment's validity plan pointed out that giving the new test days before the official one would be a practice intervention on the very test it was being validated against (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/red-team/RED_TEAM_FINDINGS.md`). The plan has every student take both tests within two weeks in counterbalanced order, so the half that sits the official test first gives a linking estimate with no prior exposure, and it offers an arm that gives the new test only after the official sitting (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/04_CONCURRENT_VALIDITY_PLAN.md`). Counterbalancing measures the practice effect rather than removing it, so the plan reports the official-score difference between the two orders as a study output. The retest literature it cites puts practice effects at about d = 0.24 to 0.26 per re-administration, and it expects format familiarity without item overlap to sit well below that.
against: Accounts differ on whether the order design was new: the package's response says the review's claim that counterbalancing was missing was a factual error (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/red-team/RED_TEAM_RESPONSE.md`). A later run found counter-evidence (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/red-team/PROTEST_BRIEF.md`).

evidence.quote: rehearsal administered days before the real test is a **practice/familiarization intervention on the criterion measure**
All students take both tests (within 2 weeks). Order is counterbalanced to control for practice effects and fatigue:
Group B (MAP-first, ~50% of the cohort) provides a linking estimate with zero prior proxy exposure by construction.
The Group A vs Group B official-MAP score difference is reported as an explicit study output: it directly estimates any practice effect of a proxy sitting on the official score
d ≈ 0.24–0.26 per re-administration, Hausknecht et al. 2007
a **post-MAP-only administration arm** is available: the proxy administered only after the official sitting.
three of its load-bearing findings rest on factual errors — a counterbalancing design it says doesn't exist
Shorter windows risk carryover from item exposure; longer windows introduce growth as a confound.
the retest literature estimates d ≈ 0.24–0.26 per re-administration
but format familiarity without item overlap should sit well below that, and the proxy contains no NWEA items
repeat sittings require retest-overlap exclusion + per-band exposure caps
a 40–43-item, MAP-format, MAP-convention rehearsal administered days before the real test is a **practice/familiarization intervention on the criterion measure**

Group B (MAP-first, ~500 students) yields a contamination-free linking estimate by construction; the Group A vs Group B official-MAP score delta is reported as an explicit study output (it directly estimates the practice effect on the criterion, turning the objection into a measured quantity).
Format familiarization without item overlap is the thing NWEA itself distributes.
